description: The plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number and accuracy for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$, with data points plotted at approximate x-values of 3, 30, 300, and 3000. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 60 to approximately 85, with tick marks at intervals of 5 units from 60 to 80. All six methods are represented by solid lines that exhibit a steady upward trend across the x-axis. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, increasing from approximately 64 at an x-value of 3 to 71 at an x-value of 3000. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, increasing from roughly 65 to 73 over the same range. The "IKE" method is depicted by a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, rising from about 67.5 to 75. The "MEMIT" method is indicated by a purple line with hexagon markers, starting at approximately 69.5 and increasing to 77.5. The "MEND" method is represented by a brown line with diamond markers, growing from roughly 71 to 80. Finally, the "ROME" method is shown as a green line with square markers, exhibiting an increase from about 74 at the start of the x-axis to 84 at the end.
